verses.text: After this, David's son Amnon fell in love with Tamar, the beautiful sister of David's son Absalom.
Amnon worked himself sick over his sister Tamar. She was a virgin, and he couldn't see how to get to her.
Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab was a shrewd man.
He asked Amnon, “Why do you look so miserable every day? You're the king's son. Won't you tell me?” Amnon answered, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”

Jonadab told him, “Get into bed and pretend you're sick. When your father visits, say, ‘Please send my sister Tamar to give me something to eat. Let her prepare it where I can see and feed me herself.’”
Amnon lay down and pretended to be sick. When the king visited, Amnon said, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make a couple of cakes where I can see her, so she can feed me herself.”
David sent word to Tamar at home: “Go to your brother Amnon's house and make him something to eat.”
So Tamar went to Amnon's house and found him lying down. She took some dough, kneaded it, shaped the cakes where he could see her, and baked them.
She tipped the cakes out of the pan in front of him, but he refused to eat. “Send everyone out,” Amnon said, and everyone left.
Then Amnon told Tamar, “Bring the food into the bedroom so you can feed me.” Tamar took the cakes she'd made and brought them into her brother's room.
When Tamar brought the food close, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me, my sister.”
“No, my brother,” she pleaded. “Don't force me. People in Israel must never do such a thing. Don't do this disgraceful thing!
Where could I go with my shame? And you'd be known as one of Israel's worst fools. Please speak to the king. He won't refuse to let you marry me.”
Amnon refused to listen. He was stronger than Tamar, and he raped her.
Then Amnon hated her. His hatred for her was stronger than the love he'd felt before. “Get up and get out!” he told her.
Tamar answered, “No! Sending me away like this is even worse than what you already did to me.” He refused to listen.
He called the servant who attended him and said, “Throw this woman out and bolt the door behind her.”
Tamar was wearing a robe of many colors, the kind the king's unmarried daughters wore. Amnon's servant put her out and bolted the door behind her.
Tamar put ashes on her head and tore her colorful robe. She put her hand on her head and went away crying out loud.
Her brother Absalom asked, “Has your brother Amnon been with you? For now, my sister, keep quiet. He's your brother. Don't take this to heart.” Tamar stayed in her brother Absalom's house, desolate.
King David heard what happened and was furious.
Absalom said nothing to Amnon, good or bad. He hated Amnon for raping his sister Tamar.
Two full years later, Absalom had sheep shearers working at Baal Hazor near Ephraim. He invited all the king's sons.
Absalom went to the king and said, “My sheep shearers are here. Please come with your servants and join me.”
The king answered, “No, my son. If we all come, we'll be a burden to you.” Absalom pressed him, but David stayed behind and gave him his blessing.
Absalom said, “If you won't come, please let my brother Amnon come with us.” The king asked, “Why should he go with you?”
Absalom kept asking until David let Amnon and all the king's sons go with him.
Absalom ordered his servants, “Watch for Amnon to get merry with wine. When I say, ‘Strike Amnon,’ kill him. Don't be afraid. I'm the one giving the order. Be brave and do it.”
Absalom's servants killed Amnon as ordered. All the other sons of the king jumped up, mounted their mules, and fled.
While they were still on the road, word reached David: “Absalom has killed all the king's sons. None of them survived!”
The king stood up, tore his clothes, and lay on the ground. All his servants stood around him with their clothes torn.
But Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah, said, “My lord, don't assume they've killed all the king's sons. Amnon alone is dead. Absalom had planned this since the day Amnon raped his sister Tamar.
So don't take it to heart, my lord the king. Your sons haven't all died. Only Amnon is dead.”
Meanwhile Absalom fled. The young man on watch looked up and saw a crowd coming down the road along the hillside behind him.
Jonadab said to the king, “Look, your sons are coming. It's just as your servant told you.”
As soon as he finished speaking, the king's sons arrived, weeping loudly. The king and all his servants wept bitterly too.
Absalom fled to Talmai son of Ammihur, the king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.
After escaping to Geshur, Absalom stayed there three years.
King David longed to go to Absalom, now that he had found some comfort after Amnon's death.
